properties.statement: CLOSED 2026-08-07, same day, by dec:sidecar-loss-guarded-by-store-evidence — the refusal now exists in code (identity::resolve_on_open + store_has_content), ver:sessions-cannot-cross-designs passes 5/5, and the whole workspace is green. Read the rest as the record of what was true inside VALID_FROM..VALID_TO; the closure is PARTIAL IN ONE NAMED WAY, which is why it is stated here rather than left to be rediscovered: the refusal STOPS the loss but does not RECOVER a design already lost, because the id can still not be read back off the store. The clause below beginning "NOT YET FIXED" described the fix that was not taken — a scan for a design under ANY id — and it was not taken because dynograph-storage exposes no such enumeration and is pinned by git tag v0.12.0, i.e. it lives in another repository. What shipped is a filesystem proxy for that scan. --- ORIGINAL RECORD FOLLOWS --- A store that loses its identity sidecar is OPENED EMPTY rather than refused, and the open destroys the evidence — the exact failure cap:hosted-state-on-a-volume forbids in its own statement ("a store without its identity sidecar is refused rather than opened empty"). Found 2026-08-07 by ver:sessions-cannot-cross-designs, written as the precondition dec:one-process-many-stores was accepted conditional on; measured, not reasoned: original id 55f9907b65553b63, id after reopen c485cd821d5a263b, real design reachable false. MECHANISM: identity lives in `<path>.id.json`, a SIBLING of the store, so the two can be parted. identity::resolve (crates/reflow2-core/src/identity.rs:126) finds no file and asks holds_default_design(), which probes ONLY for a design under DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID (graph.rs:146-148). That probe is the legacy migration path and CANNOT SEE A MINTED DESIGN BY CONSTRUCTION — every design created since identity landed is under a minted id. So the probe answers false, a NEW id is minted, and resolve() WRITES IT to the sidecar (identity.rs:171). The design is still on disk, now unreachable because graph_id namespaces every stored key, and the id needed to reach it has been overwritten. The graph then reports itself healthy and empty; nothing errors. THE SHARPENING, found by propagating chg:isolation-check-written rather than by reading code: this capability IS ALREADY BUILT — art:dockerfile realizes it, satisfying req:hosted-state-outlives-the-image — and THE DOCKERFILE ALREADY DOCUMENTS THIS EXACT FAILURE IN CAPITALS, at Dockerfile:78-82: "THE SIDECARS ARE NOT OPTIONAL AND NOT SEPARABLE. A store opened without the identity sidecar it was created with finds nothing and PRESENTS AS AN EMPTY DESIGN, reporting nothing wrong. Because they sit beside the store rather than inside it, mounting only `.../graph` and not its parent directory is a plausible-looking mistake that silently loses a project. MOUNT THE PARENT." So the failure mode was known, written down, and mitigated with A COMMENT ASKING THE OPERATOR NOT TO MAKE THE MISTAKE — while the capability the Dockerfile realizes says the store must be REFUSED rather than opened empty. The design says enforce it in code; what shipped was a warning. A mis-scoped `-v` is not an exotic input, and the operator who makes it is the one person who cannot see the warning, because it is in the image's source rather than in the error they get — which is no error at all. ADJACENCY THAT SHOWS THE RULE WAS ALREADY KNOWN IN CODE TOO: an UNREADABLE sidecar is correctly refused with "reflow2 will not guess" (identity.rs:138-145, tested at tests/design_identity.rs:139), so corrupt was refused and ABSENT was not — and absent is the more likely of the two on a volume.
